findings.evidence: grep `rw [liftFromSource_projectFromSource] at h` matches lines 744, 753, 762, 771, each followed by the identical `rw [h]; simp`.
findings.fix: State those two decomposition lemmas once. Derive the `map_*` lemmas from them with `simp [that_lemma]`, and the `mem_*` lemmas from the `map_*` ones or by `simp`.
findings.issue: The same `have h := vertices_/arrows_liftFromSource …; rw [liftFromSource_projectFromSource] at h; rw [h]; simp` block is repeated in `mem_vertices_projectFromSource`, `map_vertices_projectFromSource`, `mem_arrows_projectFromSource` and `map_arrows_projectFromSource` (lines 744, 753, 762, 771). It hides the reusable equations `p.vertices = inr false :: (projectFromSource p).2.vertices.map inl` and `p.arrows = ⟨_, _, source _⟩ :: (projectFromSource p).2.arrows.map originalArrow`.

findings.fix: Add `vertices_eq_liftWalk_projectWalk`-style decompositions (`p.vertices = inr false :: (projectWalk p).2.2.vertices.map inl ++ [inr true]`, and the same for arrows) and derive all four lemmas from them uniformly.
findings.issue: The same duplication appears for the two-terminal projection in `mem_vertices_projectWalk`, `map_vertices_projectWalk` and `map_arrows_projectWalk` (lines 851, 860, 877). Meanwhile `mem_arrows_projectWalk` uses a different route, so the four sibling proofs are inconsistent.

findings.evidence: Line 50: `simp only [projectWalk_liftWalk, Sigma.mk.inj_iff, heq_eq_eq, true_and] at hproj`. The same chain appears in the library proof of `liftWalk_injective`.
findings.fix: Replace the `hproj` derivation with `have hproj := liftWalk_injective _ _ h` (or `rw [Ne, liftWalk_inj]`), then compare arrows.
findings.issue: `parallel_loops_ne` re-proves injectivity of lifting by hand: it applies `congrArg projectWalk` and then runs `simp only [projectWalk_liftWalk, Sigma.mk.inj_iff, heq_eq_eq, true_and]`. This bypasses the exported `liftWalk_inj`/`liftWalk_injective` that the example is meant to exercise, and the hand-written `simp only` chain is brittle.

summary: Proofs are robust and the single `change` is documented, but one four-line transport pattern is copy-pasted seven times instead of being stated once as the characteristic equation it encodes. One example also re-derives `liftWalk_injective` by hand.
